lens_summary.drift: m9-76 closes FIND-M9-73-CC4-REGEN-RITUAL-NOT-IN-REPO, the low process finding confirmed a fifth time in m9-75 and re-confirmed during this cycle. CC#4 checks artifact-index SHA-256 consistency across archive manifests from scripts/check_vault_drift.sh, but its repair half lived only in the agent scratch directory: a throwaway python script re-derived each cycle whose naive whole-tree form churned the self-referential rows of the pre-m9-11 manifests, which then had to be reverted by hand. The consequence worth naming is epistemic, not merely ergonomic - the gate's logic was never exercised by the tool meant to satisfy it, which is how the broken awk of m9-66 stayed invisible for many cycles. The cycle lands scripts/regen_manifest_index_shas.py as the repair half, deliberately mirroring CC#4's two edge rules because agreement with the gate is the whole justification for the tool: the self-referential row is preserved (a file cannot contain its own hash; CC#4 skips it by path comparison) and a row whose target file no longer exists is left byte-for-byte untouched and reported as missing (CC#4 guards every comparison with [ -f "$path" ], so a dangling row is invisible to it). No flags rewrites to a bounded fixpoint, because rewriting one manifest changes the bytes of any manifest another lists; --check writes nothing and exits 1 naming each stale row, which is the machine proof that the ritual ran; --dry-run reports and exits 0; --verbose lists untouched manifests. scripts/tests/test_regen_manifest_index_shas.py adds 13 zero-dependency unittest cases, including the fixpoint across two manifests that list each other and the preservation of dangling rows. scripts/smoke_test_ccs.sh gains a sixth check with four phases - unit tests pass, --check clean on a clean clone, injected drift flagged by both --check and CC#4 with the row named, and the rewrite restoring the true SHA with both green again - and setup_work_copy now overlays the working-tree vault tooling so the suite exercises the tree about to merge rather than HEAD alone, which had cost m9-75 a wasted run. The tool was used on its own cycle: editing the smoke script, the drift-sweep doc and AGENTS.md staled rows in six historical manifests plus two more, and one fixpoint command plus --check replaced the hand ritual, with no manual revert of self rows needed. Falsification ran guard by guard - quiet-gating the stale-row print (this one was hit organically and is why the naming test exists), removing the self-row comparison (the tool then tries to write a manifest's own hash into itself and two tests fail), disabling --check's failure branch, removing the dangling-row guard, reducing the loop to a single pass, and writing a wrong hash (which fails through the loop bound, not the SHA assertion) - each restored byte-identically against a scratch backup. Two limits are recorded rather than papered over: phase (d)'s true-SHA assertion was never observed to be the failing line because the fixpoint bound fires first for any wrong repair, and the dangling-row rule is only observable under a mutation that blanks and counts the row, since the inert variant is a no-op. CC counts are unchanged at 48 python + 7 bash, because CC#4 already covers SHA consistency and a duplicate check would be noise.

evidence.falsification: Six mutations, each reverted and cmp-verified byte-identical against /home/rubentxu/.jcode/scratch/regen.m9-76-good.py before the next: (1) quiet-gated stale-row print -> test_stale_row_is_named_in_check_output FAILED and the smoke suite FAILED with 'regen: --check did not name the drifted row' (hit organically on the first smoke run, which is why the test exists); (2) self-row comparison removed -> test_clean_manifest_exits_zero and test_self_row_is_preserved FAILED and the real tree reported a self row as stale; (3) --check failure branch disabled -> two unit tests FAILED and the smoke suite FAILED; (4) dangling-row guard removed -> FileNotFoundError, and the blanks-and-counts variant -> test_missing_target_is_preserved_and_invisible_to_check FAILED with '1 != 0'; (5) single-pass loop -> test_fixpoint_across_interlinked_manifests FAILED; (6) wrong hash written -> smoke FAILED with 'regen: rewrite exit=2 (expected 0)' through the loop bound.

subject.fix: scripts/regen_manifest_index_shas.py: ROW regex matching CC#4's row shape; sha256() streaming; default_manifests(root) discovering .sddk-knowledge/*/changes/archive/*/archive-manifest.md; rows_of(); rewrite(manifest, root, write) with the two preservation rules (self row by normalized-path equality, dangling row untouched and reported); main() with --check (exit 1 naming stale rows), --dry-run (exit 0), --verbose, and a bounded fixpoint loop (MAX_PASSES = 5) because rewriting one manifest changes the bytes of any manifest another lists. scripts/tests/test_regen_manifest_index_shas.py: 13 unittest cases, no third-party dependency. scripts/smoke_test_ccs.sh: test_regen_script() sixth check with four phases, plus setup_work_copy() overlaying the working-tree regen script and its tests. subject.gap: scripts/check_vault_drift.sh implements CC#4 (artifact-index SHA-256 rows must match the current file content, self-referential row excluded). The repair side had no home in the repository: each cycle re-derived a throwaway python script in /home/rubentxu/.jcode/scratch/, and the naive whole-tree version churned the self-referential rows of the manifests written before m9-11, which had to be reverted by hand. Two consequences: the gate's own logic was never exercised by the tool meant to satisfy it, so the broken awk of m9-66 accumulated silent drift for many cycles; and the ritual was invisible to reviewers, who could neither re-run it nor tell a correctly regenerated table from a hand-edited one. Deferred four times (m9-72, m9-73, m9-74, m9-75) as process friction behind product work.

The self-row and dangling-row rules now have one implementation instead of a per-cycle re-derivation.
